audit.why: Both layers already read Skill / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Skill / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia, which is exactly what the mirror audit set and what the packet chart says. audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike, the mid text and the do's all hang on cooldowns that are never numbered — only Miasma's 24s appears anywhere.
audit.why: Hijack is 80s at rank 1 and 30s at rank 3, Abscond/Abduct is 13s at rank 1, and Miasma's 16-24s is the actual gap you step into. Numbers turn 'wait for the window' into a countable action.
audit.corrected: Miasma's 16-24s added to dosFull[0].d, Abscond's 13s to spikes[0], Hijack's 80s to the mid text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twin Fang is described purely as damage — 'chains every poison tick into bonus damage'. Riot's text also heals her for a percentage of the damage dealt, and nothing in the entry names Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: Her sustain, not just her DPS, is what wins the levels 3-5 attrition war the entry tells you to survive; anti-heal timing is the decision the player actually has to make.
audit.corrected: Twin Fang's heal named in whys[3] with Grievous Wounds as the answer. Miasma's grounding of both Abscond and the Kingslayer lunge stated explicitly in dosFull[0].d — Riot's own W text says grounded enemies cannot use movement abilities, so this one is safe to assert.

audit.why: Petrifying Gaze's facing rule is already stated correctly in whys[4], spikes[1], mid and wants.you[2] — enemies facing her are stunned, the rest are slowed, which is why a Hijacked cast has to be aimed at her front.

edits.before: The 54% win rate comes from your level 6 spike, not lane dominance — Cassiopeia beats you in levels 3-5 through pure sustained poke that chips you below the W heal threshold before you can get close. Play patient, stack passive charges on safe farm, and wait for Miasma to hit cooldown before every step-up. At 6, Hijack gives you her Petrifying Gaze: if you can E2 hook her and face her direction as you cast it, you face-stun her into the full Q-W-passive burst and she dies. This is your lane-winning window, but if she has a point in Miasma ready she will still Ground the E2 and force you back — respect it every time.
edits.after: The 54% win rate comes from your level 6 spike, not lane dominance — Cassiopeia beats you in levels 3-5 with poke that chips you below the W heal threshold, and Twin Fang refunds it to her while she does it. Play patient, stack Petricite charges on safe farm, and step up only in Miasma's 16-24s gap. At 6, Hijack gives you Petrifying Gaze on an 80s clock: E2 hook her, cast it into her face so the stun lands rather than the slow, and the Q-W-passive burst finishes it. That is your lane-winning window — but a ready Miasma still grounds the E2 and sends you back, so check it every time.

edits.before: Once Cassiopeia completes Seraph's Embrace into Shadowflame her Twin Fang DPS outruns your W healing in a sustained fight; she simply cycles E on poisoned targets faster than you can recover HP. Your path to winning the late game is converting the level 6 kill lead into dragon or tower and ending before 30 minutes. If the game goes long, play teamfight angles — E2 onto her backline, steal Petrifying Gaze to peel, and never 1v1 her at full build without her R already on cooldown.
edits.after: Once Cassiopeia completes Seraph's Embrace into Shadowflame her Twin Fang cycles outrun your W healing and top her up at the same time; without Grievous Wounds the sustained fight is unwinnable. Your path is converting the level 6 kill lead into dragon or tower and ending before 30 minutes. If the game goes long, play teamfight angles — E2 onto her backline, steal Petrifying Gaze to peel, and never 1v1 her at full build with her 80s R up.

notes: This entry was in better shape than the rest of the shard — chart already matched the mirror, Miasma's grounding and Petrifying Gaze's facing rule were both stated correctly, and the mid text already explains the win-rate-versus-chart tension the packet flags as a defect.
